summary: ```# Marvelous Designer Official Tutorial Video: Introduction to Animation Production ## Overview This tutorial provides a step-by-step guide on how to utilize animation features in Marvelous Designer, including importing models, setting up animations, and making adjustments for realistic clothing simulations. ## Input Menu First, at the bottom of the file menu in the main menu, you can find the input menu. You can choose FBX or Alembic files according to your needs. Remember to select the animation, catch animation, and auto-generate setting. ## Importing Models After entering the model file with the action, you can see the action of the character in the animation mode. You need to record the animation in this mode. There is a setting near the virtual model that you can adjust. In different actions, the actual posture may vary, and sometimes it becomes more challenging to fit the clothes properly. Therefore, we can first select the animation, catch animation, and auto-generate setting. Then, save the actual model as an OBJ as a backup. When saving, remember to check the selection option. ### Preparing the T-Pose Model I have prepared an OBJ model in a T-pose. It is also exported again in the software to ensure that these two models have the same face number. As long as the face number is consistent, you can perform morph target operations. Afterward, import the T-pose model to wear clothes. ## Adjusting the Model After opening the setting point, you will notice that the setting point has been re-created and does not fit the virtual model. In the virtual model editor, you can modify the properties of the setting boards in the settings column. Once the modification is complete, select the setting board in the 3D window and adjust it using the positioning ball. The setting board represents the shape that will form when arranged on the setting point. Subsequent adjustments are based on this setting board. ### Saving the Setting Board After adjusting the model's setting board, you can save it for reuse on similar models in the future. As long as this model is re-saved as a virtual model, the next time you open it, it will retain the setting board information. ## Importing Clothing Now, double-click to import a set of pre-set clothes. Since we are going to use the transform function later, to save time during the transformation, we will first increase all the clothing examples. After increasing, we will simulate it. ### Simulating and Adjusting Clothing After stabilizing, select the OBJ file to be imported. For the type of import, choose Morph Target. Upon importing, the model will be transformed, and its posture will be altered. Next, some basic adjustments need to be made to these clothing examples. Start by reducing the surface diameter of the model to 1. The surface diameter refers to the air thickness around the model. Reducing this value can make the clothing appear more realistic. Additionally, reduce the conflict density of the model. Furthermore, we need to decrease the overall size of the clothing example. This adjustment will enhance the stability of the clothing during the production process, resulting in more detailed rendering. For smaller models, it's best to reduce the size of the example to 3 or less. ### Finalizing the Model After the costume is finished, delete the model. Then, enter the file with the action. Remember to reduce the surface diameter to 1 since you've changed to a new model. Switch to animation mode and prepare to record the animation. ## Recording Animation Click the recording button in the lower-left corner to start recording the animation. During the process, you can click record again to pause. In animation mode, the model type will change to a more stable but time-consuming finished model. To ensure the quality of the animation, do not change the model preset. ### Playback and Adjustments After recording, drag the playback bar back to the starting position to play again. You may notice that the hat part will hang on the shoulder at the end of the recording. Check the play area to identify where the animation needs to be altered. If recording has not started, you can turn on the simulation to adjust the simulation effect. Adjust the current frame rate, and find the specific frame that requires slight modifications in the clothing shape. ### Editing the Animation After changing the format, click again to record and copy the previous animation. This editing method is more suitable for projects where computer operation speed is low during animation recording. Another method involves manually dragging the costume while recording the animation for a more natural effect. If the simulation result is not ideal after covering, you can delete it. ### Important Notes Once you start recording the animation, avoid returning to the usual simulation mode to make changes to the version. If the grid changes, the animation will need to be recorded from the beginning. After deleting, you can retain the original animation. ## Exporting the Animation After recording, you can export the animation. It is recommended to export it in Alembic format. When exporting, you have the option to include the model with the mushroom model. ## Conclusion After editing, you can quickly review what you've accomplished and showcase it at the end of the video. Once you finish the video, you can return to different functions as needed. ```
